reasons: Claimed status is compliant-at-fallback with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals.

The cited text supports the classification: ¶4(a) grants 'Either Party' (Customer is a defined 'Party' per p0000) a no-cause right to terminate 'for any reason' following the Initial Term on 90 days' written notice — within the fallback's 60–90 day band.
Walk-away is not triggered: the Initial Term is one (1) year (not a multi-year lock-out), and Vendor's convenience right is on 90 days' notice, i.e. not 'fewer than 90 days'.

No early-termination fee or penalty; Kubient's entitlement to fees generated during the 90-day notice period is earned revenue share, not an exit charge, and is at or under the 3-months'-fees fallback cap.
The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is adequately explained as a phrasing artefact ('Either Party' rather than 'Customer'), not a substantive gap.

Shortfalls versus preferred (90 vs 30 days' notice, Vendor exit not limited to end of term, no pro-rata prepaid refund under a pure revenue-share model) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than escalated to a deviation, consistent with the playbook's minor sub-element guidance.
